intro.title: Northeast China, Season by Season
intro.left: Northeast China spans Liaoning, Jilin, and Heilongjiang. Its cities carry Manchurian history, industrial memory, Russian architectural influence, Korean cultural connections, and some of the country’s most distinctive winter traditions.
intro.right: This is not one compact destination. A good route chooses a clear seasonal story: Harbin and snow country in winter, Changbai Mountain and forest landscapes in autumn, or Shenyang and Dalian for heritage, coast, and city life. The distances make pacing more important than collecting stops.

stay.title: How long to stay
stay.summary: Choose two or three bases and leave room for weather, long transfers, and full outdoor days.

plans.label: 5 days
plans.summary: Focus on Harbin and one nearby winter area, with enough time for the city beyond the ice festival.

plans.label: 7 days
plans.summary: Combine Harbin with Changbai Mountain or Shenyang for a clearer contrast between nature and history.

plans.label: 10 days
plans.summary: Connect Harbin, Changbai Mountain, Shenyang, and Dalian with realistic transfer days.

items.label: Route scale
items.summary: Northeast China is a large region. High-speed rail helps between major cities, while mountain and snow areas require road transfers.

items.label: Winter weather
items.summary: Harbin can be extremely cold. Proper insulated boots, gloves, face protection, and spare phone batteries are essential.

items.label: Season matters
items.summary: Ice attractions and snow villages are winter products; mountain access, color, and daylight vary significantly by month.

items.label: Where to begin
items.summary: Use Harbin for a winter-first route, Shenyang for history, or Dalian for a milder coastal introduction.
